summary: All parts of the request (sentence count and average, definition of sentence/word, empty text, TypeError) map to REQ-001..003, with concrete and computable acceptance criteria (verified arithmetic of AC-001-1..5). Ambiguities (tail text, repeated punctuation, abbreviations) are recorded as assumptions. Only minor gaps remain: ASM-003/ASM-004 behaviours have no acceptance criteria.

checklist.item: Every part of the request covered
checklist.note: Function, sentence/word definitions, empty/whitespace, TypeError all covered.
REQ-001..003 have concrete input/output examples; REQ-004 is a constraint checkable by inspection.
Expected values recomputed and consistent with the stated rules.
Stdlib-only captured (REQ-004); no performance need stated by the request.

checklist.item: Critical decisions escalated to the user
checklist.note: No security or data-loss decisions; non-interactive run noted in ASM-005 for post-hoc confirmation.
ASM-001..005 conservative and record their impact.

findings.description: ASM-003 (consecutive punctuation, punctuation-only segments like '...' or 'Hi. ... Bye.') and ASM-004 (mid-sentence period like '3.14' splits sentences) have no acceptance criteria, so these behaviours may go untested at system level.
REQ-001 says words are separated by whitespace ('공백') while REQ-002 lists space/tab/newline; whether Unicode whitespace is included is not stated (ASM-004 implies str.split).
ASM-002 (unterminated tail not counted) is a literal reading but is a user-visible choice; user should confirm later.
